text: Write a class with a static factory method instead of a public constructor, and one thing a constructor cannot do. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___ { this.celsius = c; }               // hidden, so callers use the factories
static Temperature fromCelsius(double c)    { return new Temperature(c); }
explanation: Verified: 100.0. Two constructors both taking a `double` would be identical signatures and would not compile, which is the concrete thing a factory buys — a *name*. It also lets you return a cached instance or a subtype, which is why `List.of`, `Integer.valueOf` and `Optional.of` are factories. Chapter 22 notes that `Integer.valueOf` caching is exactly why `==` on boxed 128 differs from `==` on boxed 127.
